intent: Bring the three over-cap cups_service test modules under the 250-line cap by partitioning them, with no change to what is tested.
scope: Non-goal: no assertion changed, no test deleted, skipped or weakened
changes: test_cups_service.py split at TestPortStatusViaUsblp: the pyusb device info and CUPS service control tests stay, the usblp ioctl port-status tests go to test_cups_service_port.py.

test_cups_service_part2.py split at TestCupsReasonsToError: economode and CUPS-state mapping stay, the error-reason mapping, port-status-to-code mapping and printer-name discovery go to test_cups_status_mapping.py.

test_cups_service_part3.py was a single 235-line class, so it split by method at test_port_ok_toner_exhausted: the no-port-status and hardware-error cases stay, the four healthy-port cases become TestQueryUsbViaCupsPortOk in test_cups_fallback_port_ok.py.
Renamed the four part-numbered files after what they actually cover: test_cups_economode.py, test_cups_fallback_query.py, test_cups_ipp.py, plus the two new names.
Import blocks trimmed per file to what each uses. No MOD constant changed; the source split in the previous commits already put every patched name in the module these files name.

verification.evidence: 402 passed before the split and 402 passed after it - identical pass count.

The first run after the part2 split reported 2 failed, 400 passed: the moved classes needed subprocess (for TimeoutExpired) and get_status_info, which my hand-written import block had dropped. Both added; the suite returned to 402. Recorded because it is exactly the failure the pass-count check exists to catch.
No cups_service or _cups_fallback test module is listed any more; brother_printer is down to five over-cap files, all of them other test modules.

verification.command: pre-commit run --files <the touched test files and artifacts>
verification.evidence: ruff, ruff format, mypy, pylint, bandit, name-tests-test and pytest-with-coverage all pass.

risks: Hand-trimmed import blocks are the live risk in this kind of split, as the two failures above show. A dropped name fails loudly at collection or call time, so the pass count catches it; the danger would be trimming an import that only a skipped test used.
Three of these files are now named after _cups_fallback rather than cups_service, matching where the code moved in an earlier commit.
rollback: git revert the commit; the three originals return at 390, 261 and 260 lines and the three new modules disappear.
After rollback, re-run the package suite and confirm it still reports 402 passed.
